title: Minimax Rates for Recurrent-Event Contrasts with Growing Panel Visits and a Terminal Event
banked_reason: Bounded Nelson–Aalen counting-process substrate construction exhausted after two ten-round study windows; five load-bearing proofs remain open, so F3 cannot complete; the mathematical claim was not refuted.
gap_reasons: The Nelson–Aalen integrated risk step needs a counting-process martingale isometry. Causalean concept, type, goal, and local searches found only general squared-risk and sample-split lemmas; Mathlib search found general martingale definitions, which do not establish the required hazard-counting identity.
Reached BUILD_CAP (10) without the scaffolder requesting review.
proof_attempt_summary: The field-tier discovery passed, and formalization advanced to F3, where the integrated censoring-risk lemma required a reusable continuous-time counting-process martingale isometry. The counting_process_nelson_aalen_isometry study exhausted its initial and one additional ten-round build window; its final build was green but retained five sorrys in the isometry and independent-random-time chain, so no review or placement occurred. This is a bounded proof-substrate failure, not a refutation of the mathematical frontier claim.
tldr: Independent inspections reveal a first-recurrence path through one categorical transition, so increasing the visit count changes information through adjacent transition categories rather than through \(nJ\) independent responses. The proved results establish matching minimax mean-squared-error and uniformly honest connected-interval-length orders \(n^{-1}+\{nJ^2\log(en)\}^{-2/3}\) and \(n^{-1/2}+\{nJ^2\log(en)\}^{-1/3}\) for every \(2\le J\le n^2\). The ambient class imposes terminal Lipschitzness but no class-wide terminal-probability interior floor; the explicit least-favorable traces are instead proved to remain in \([1/4,3/4]\). A fully piecewise complete-death transition statistic attains the frontier without learning the unrestricted death-specific trace. Cross-fitted censor weighting is controlled by an integrated Nelson--Aalen risk bound that uses the censor-survival floor to bound total cumulative hazard and requires neither a pointwise hazard ceiling nor a death-time density. The complete categorical Kullback--Leibler calculation for the specified least-favorable pair gives the rate-level converse.
gap: Fixed-two-visit interval-censoring theory establishes the classical logarithm, and fixed-law mixed-case theory does not expose how its constants evolve when the deterministic visit count grows with sample size. Reversed-mean panel-count methods additionally pool death times through a homogeneous gap function.
fill: The project derives the all-category information modulus, constructs a matching within-person transition estimator, locates the root-\(n\) saturation boundary, and matches the worst-case length of uniformly honest connected intervals under estimated censor survival.
